deal.name: NorthBridge Bank — Platform evaluation (corrected run)
deal.note: Identical call, same buyer, same questions. The rep now says only what the documentation supports. Run the two side by side to see what the bot changed.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: Thanks for making time. Quick context: we're a regulated bank, about four thousand staff, and our regulators have become much stricter about where customer data physically sits.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: That is exactly the deployment we are built for. IOMETE was founded in 2021, and the platform has been self-hosted on Kubernetes from the start.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: The platform is built on Apache Spark for compute with Apache Iceberg as the table format, and it is deployed on Kubernetes.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: And where does our data actually live? Our security team will ask that in the first ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: The platform operates entirely within your infrastructure, so no data is sent outside your organization. That includes the control plane, not only the compute.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: You can also run the whole thing air-gapped if you need to, with no outbound internet at all.

utterances.speaker: buyer2
utterances.text: That helps. What about SSO? We're on Okta and we use SCIM for provisioning.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: SAML and OIDC with Okta, and SCIM provisioning, are all supported out of the box.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: Our current warehouse takes four hours to produce the daily risk report. Every morning it's still running when the desk opens.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Iceberg tables accumulate small files and metadata as they grow, which is the usual reason a job like that slows down quarter over quarter. Compaction and orphan file cleanup run as a built-in service, so query times do not degrade over time.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: Who does that maintenance, us or you?

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: It ships as a service in the platform with configurable thresholds, and the maintenance operations are documented end to end if your team wants to run them directly.

utterances.speaker: buyer2
utterances.text: Our security review needs SOC 2 Type II and a penetration test summary before we're even allowed to start a POC.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: I won't guess at that one — the product docs do not carry the attestations, so I'll send the trust-centre link and the current report in writing today.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: And budget. Ballpark, what does this cost for forty terabytes?

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: I'd rather not improvise a number on a call. I'll send a written quote with the sizing assumptions so your finance team can check it line by line.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: Okay. What would a POC look like in practice?

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Two weeks. One namespace on your Kubernetes, we load one real table, you run the risk report query and compare it yourself.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: Can we time-travel to see what the data looked like at month end, for the audit trail?

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Yes, Iceberg snapshot time travel lets you query as of a timestamp or a snapshot ID. Auditors tend to like that one.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: Last thing. Does this lock us in? Our board is sensitive after the last vendor.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: No. It's an open table format, Iceberg, so your data stays as Parquet files in your own bucket even if you leave.

utterances.speaker: buyer
utterances.text: Good. Send me the security documentation and a one-pager I can take to the risk committee on Thursday.
